hypotheses.statement: Sustained higher u increases steady-state y (positive DC gain).
Y responds to u with lag/delay of several seconds and settles over 10-20s, not instantly.
Inputs below u~0.2 produce no measurable rise (dead zone at low input).
At u=0, y decays toward near zero due to self-drainage.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u in [0,1].
Holding y=0.6 at steady state requires u in range 0.3-0.7.
Sensor noise on y is zero-mean with std below 0.02.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Direction and magnitude of gain plus response lag, which determines what steady input can hold 0.6 and what controller gain and timing are feasible.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no drain or lag: 0.3816 + 0.10*0.4*10.0 = 0.7816 which stays below soft limit 0.85 and hard cutoff 0.9.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive gain with lag is correct, y rises from ~0.38 toward ~0.5 with a delay of a few seconds, positive slope that flattens if approaching equilibrium, plus small noise.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero completed experiments: gain magnitude, lag, deadzone, u=0 decay rate, linearity, u-needed-for-0.6, and noise are all unresolved, so a controller cannot be justified yet; need at least three experiments.
proposal.operator_note: Probing with mid pump duty to measure rise rate and lag.

Change is weaker actuator: same u produces smaller rise and lower steady y with unchanged drain rate and delay.
Change is faster outflow: fall at u=0 is faster and same u holds lower y with unchanged actuator gain and delay.
Change is slower response / longer delay: first response delayed by >5s vs 2-4s before and approach slower, causing oscillation under old controller.
Change is sensor shift: y offset or markedly different noise vs before.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Directly measure post-change input delay and u=0 fall rate to discriminate longer delay/slower approach (C3) from weaker gain (C1), faster drain (C2), or sensor shift (C4), which sets safe controller timing and feedforward.
proposal.safety_argument: With u=0 the commanded worst-case rise RATE*u*duration is zero so this hold cannot drive the level higher; level starts at 0.982 under forced u=0 since ~116s so in-transit high-u effects have largely elapsed and the level will drain downward, minimizing time near the hard cutoff; this is the minimum-inflow safe action.
proposal.expected_observation: If longer delay (C3) is right, y will hold/creep briefly for several seconds from in-transit effects then fall steadily at ~0.015-0.035/s toward ~0.3-0.5 over 40s with small +/-0.01 noise; distinctly faster fall would favour C2, markedly weak rise history favours C1, persistent offset or changed noise favours C4.
proposal.readiness_justification: No controlled after-change experiment completed yet; delay, gain, drain and sensor uncertainties remain unresolved from observational traces alone, so a controller cannot be justified; a u=0 drain cleanly resolves delay while improving safety, which is acceptable to do first.
proposal.operator_note: Holding pump off to drain from high level while measuring delay and drain rate.

submission.machine_card: Reservoir, positive gain: higher u raises level. Lag: 2-4s pure delay (E4 kept rising 1.2s after u->0, E5 flat 2-3s after u->0.6) plus slow first-order tau ~30s near 0.6 (slopes 0.020 at y0.22 to 0.0074 at y0.60 under u=0.6) and ~12-14s near drain (u=0 slope -0.029 at y0.41, -0.019 at y0.16). Gain nonlinear: u=0.4 equilibrium ~0.25-0.28 (E1 0.38->0.28 slope still -0.003), u=0.6 equilibrium ~0.80-0.83 (extrapolated, still +0.0074 at 0.615), u=0.7 eq >1.0 (still +0.021 at 0.54). Fits deadzone dz~0.30 K~2.7. Self-draining: u=0 falls 0.56->0.12 in 19s toward ~0. Dead zone below ~0.2-0.3 suspected but low confidence. Noise zero-mean +-0.01, std <0.02. Hold for 0.6 needs u~0.52 (interpolated between +0.009 at u0.6 and -0.010 at u0.4), not 0.60 (0.60 still rising). Worst rate 0.08/unit/s.
submission.design_rationale: Evidence shows positive gain with 2-4s delay and long self-draining tau. u=0.4 drives y down to ~0.28 (E1) and from 0.62 down at -0.010/s (E12); u=0.6 drives y from 0.12 to 0.615 over 42s with slope falling 0.020 to 0.0074 (E5-E10); u=0 decays to ~0.12 with tau ~12-14s (E4); u=0.7 still rising +0.02/s at 0.5 (E2-E3). First-order fit to u=0.6 gives y_eq~0.82 tau~30s, while u=0.4 eq~0.25 implies strong nonlinearity/deadzone. Linearized deadzone fit y_eq=K*(u-dz) gives dz~0.30 K~2.7. Zero-crossing of slope at y~0.58: u=0.6 +0.0093/s vs u=0.4 -0.0104/s interpolates to u_eq~0.52 for 0.6. Hence feedforward ff=0.297+target/2.72 (~0.517 at 0.6). PI corrects residual: Kp=0.55 gives loop gain ~0.8-1.5 without exciting 3s delay, Ki=0.10 Ti~5.5s corrects 0.05 error in ~10-15s within 30s settling window. Integral gated to |e|<0.20 and clamped to +-0.25 leaves authority for ff error up to 0.25 (covers H6 0.55-0.70 uncertainty) while preventing windup during initial far approach. 1.5s EMA suppresses +-0.01 noise (std<0.02). 0.85 max and 0.75/0.80 safety caps prevent 0.9 hard cutoff given max rate 0.08/s.
submission.predicted_behavior: From low level, saturates near 0.79-0.85 then glides into band in ~25-35s; from near band, enters 0.55-0.65 within ~10s and stays. Settles to 0.60 +-0.02 with <0.03 overshoot in true state, no ringing above 0.65 and far from 0.85/0.9. Steady duty ~0.51-0.55 for 0.6 target, integral trims any 0.1 feedforward miss within settling window. Time in band after 30s >85% in nominal plant.
self_test_expectations: control returns finite float in [0,1] on first call with {} and on noisy y, varying dt 0.02-1.0s, never raises.
With yf=0.60 target 0.60 output ~0.47-0.57 (feedforward +- integral clamp) not saturated.
With y=0.10 target 0.60 output >0.65 and <0.86 (proportional boost, no windup).
With yf=0.82 output 0.0 (high safety) and integral bled non-positive.
State stays small JSON with yf and integ only, integ bounded within +-0.25.
Repeated calls at steady 0.60 converge u to 0.45-0.62 without oscillation >0.1.
submission.operator_note: Controller holds ~0.52 duty near target and trims with PI. Starts pumping ~0.79 from low level, eases to ~0.53 in band. Filtered measurement rides through noise. Safety caps duty if filtered level exceeds 0.75-0.80 to stay clear of 0.9 cutoff. Expect slow 20-30s approach with no aggressive surges; leave it alone to settle. Energy is modest: steady ~0.52.

submission.diagnosis: Deadtime/lag increased ~7x, gain/drain/sensor essentially unchanged. Nominal: E5 0->0.6 step flat ~3s then 0.0199/s rise; E2 0.4->0.7 lag ~2s. Post: E14 0->0.5 from rest flat 16s at 0.0001/s with noise <0.008; continuation E15 stays <0.01 until ~182.2s then breaks at 0.016/s. Total deadtime 159.9 to 182.2 = ~22.3s. Post-onset slope 0.016 at u=0.5 scales with nominal 0.02 at u=0.6, so actuator gain unchanged within ~20%. E13 u=0 fall starts immediately at -0.035/s high-level comparable to nominal E4, and zero reading/noise unchanged, ruling out outflow increase or sensor shift. Old PI with Kp0.55/Ki0.10 designed for 3s goes unstable with 22s, producing observed limit cycle 0.1-0.9 and hard violations.
submission.change_summary: Kept feedforward+PI structure but made it delay-tolerant: added latched slow-delay detector (~8s of drive without response), dual gain sets (fast Kp0.45/Ki0.055 vs slow Kp0.16/Ki0.012), slew limits (0.25/s fast, 0.04/s slow), Umax 0.82/0.68, slow feedforward trim, and predictive braking y_pred=yf+yd*Td gated on yf>0.55. This prevents integral windup and in-flight overshoot that caused 0.9+ violations under 22s deadtime while preserving nominal drive.
submission.machine_card: Reservoir y in [0,1], u in [0,1]. Nominal: first-order + deadtime Td~2-4s, Tau~15-20s, DC gain K~1.0 (u=0.6 holds ~0.60-0.63, u=0 drains to 0). Post-change: Td~22s for pump path (22.3s measured E14+E15), Tau/K/drain/noise unchanged. Control implication: need bandwidth <0.02 rad/s equivalent, Umax~0.68, slew~0.04/s, predictor horizon 22s when yf>0.55. Target 0.6 band 0.55-0.65, soft 0.85 hard 0.9.
submission.design_rationale: Old failure is classic deadtime instability: controller kept integrating/pumping while y was stale, then 22s of stored pump arrived at once. Fix must (1) detect deadtime online, (2) lower bandwidth so loop crossover <<1/Td, (3) limit rate and ceiling of u to bound in-flight energy, (4) brake early using y+yd*Td when already near band. Fast mode preserves nominal 2-4s performance; slow mode gives closed-loop Tc>>22s. Feedforward ~0.52 does most work so low slow gains still hold 0.6. Gated predictor avoids stalling far below target.
submission.predicted_behavior: Delayed 22s plant: u rises to ~0.60-0.65 then backs to ~0.52 within 10s of detection, y starts moving ~22s after step, climbs at ~0.01-0.016/s without overshoot beyond ~0.72, settles 0.55-0.65, zero hard violations, in-band after 30s >0.6 vs 0.126 before, MAE ~0.06-0.09 vs 0.20 before. Nominal 3s plant: rise similar to before (u~0.64 initial), settle 0.60 +/-0.03, MAE ~0.035-0.05, in-band >0.70, no overrides.
